sentiment.rationale: The document shows strong operational momentum with record revenues in all five businesses and positive operating leverage for the firm and each business for the second straight year. Management explicitly raised the 2026 NII ex-Markets guidance to 5-6% growth (from a prior expectation of a slowdown) and targets a ~60% efficiency ratio and another year of positive operating leverage. The CEO states they are 'committed to reaching our target of 10-11% RoTCE for the year' and enter 2026 with 'visible momentum.' While the Q4 reported results were mixed due to a large Russia-related notable item, the adjusted results and forward guidance represent a meaningful upward trajectory. The score is capped at +0.30 because the formal 2026 RoTCE target of 10-11% was previously stated and is being reaffirmed, not raised, and the efficiency ratio target was slightly softened from 'below 60%' to 'around 60%' to allow for continued investment.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 reported revenues of $19.9 billion, up 2% YoY. Excluding the Russia notable item, revenues were up 8% to $21.0 billion. Full year 2025 reported revenues of $85.2 billion, up 6% YoY. Excluding notable items, revenues were $86.4 billion, up 7% YoY.
summary.eps: Q4 2025 diluted EPS of $1.19, down 11% YoY from $1.34. Excluding the Russia notable item, EPS was $1.81. Full year 2025 diluted EPS of $6.99, up 18% YoY from $5.94. Excluding notable items, full year EPS was $7.97.
summary.guidance: Management expects 2026 NII ex-Markets to be up 5-6% YoY. They target a ~60% efficiency ratio and another year of positive operating leverage. They reaffirm the target of 10-11% RoTCE for 2026. They expect card NCLs to remain within the 2025 ranges (Branded Cards: 3.50%-4.00%; Retail Services: 5.75%-6.25%). They will continue to buy back shares against the $20 billion buyback program.
summary.margin: Efficiency ratio (total operating expenses/total revenues, net) was 69.6% in Q4 2025, up 250 bps YoY. For the full year 2025, the efficiency ratio was 64.7%, improving 170 bps YoY. On an adjusted basis (excluding notable items), the full year 2025 efficiency ratio was 63.0%. Management targets an efficiency ratio of ~60% for 2026.
key_risks: Russia notable item: A $1.2 billion pre-tax loss ($1.1 billion after-tax) related to the held-for-sale accounting treatment of Citi's plan to sell AO Citibank in Russia.
Macroeconomic uncertainty: The document notes potential impacts from slowing economic growth, elevated unemployment, inflation, changes in interest rates, and geopolitical tensions.
Regulatory risk: The consent order from the OCC remains in place, and the timing of its closure is uncertain and 'up to the regulators.'
Credit risk: Corporate non-accrual loans increased 45% YoY to $2.0 billion, driven by idiosyncratic downgrades in Banking and Services. Consumer non-accrual loans increased 24% YoY to $1.6 billion.
Competitive gap: The CEO acknowledged a gap versus best-in-class peers in Investment Banking and capital markets, requiring continued investment.
key_opportunities: Record revenues in all five businesses (Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth, USPB) in 2025.
Strong momentum in Services with 8% revenue growth (ex-notable item), driven by higher deposit balances and fee growth.
Banking had a record year for M&A revenues and gained wallet share, with a rich pipeline entering 2026.
Wealth delivered 14% revenue growth and 8% organic NNIA growth, with a long-term EBT margin target of 25-30%.
USPB returns more than doubled to mid-teens, driven by product innovation and customer engagement.
Capital return: Returned over $17.5 billion to shareholders in 2025, with plans to continue buybacks against a $20 billion program.
Transformation progress: Over 80% of programs are at or near target state, with the OCC removing Article 17 of the Consent Order, signaling improved safety and soundness.
AI deployment: Over 180K colleagues using AI tools, generating 100K hours of capacity weekly, expected to drive future efficiencies.
